title: Angle reasoning practice sheet (lesson 65)
subject: Mathematics
unit: Summer 1: Geometric notation and constructions; geometric reasoning
source: Seeded from mathematics/y7 lesson 65 (Angle reasoning practice sheet (portal worksheet for this lesson))
intro: Lesson 65: Angle problems: lines, points and equations. To understand how to combine angle facts at lines and points to solve multi-step problems with reasons

model.title: Two lines cross. One angle is 2x and its neighbour is x + 30. Find x and all four angles.

parts.label: Step 1
parts.text: Neighbours on a straight line: 2x + x + 30 = 180

model.title: Angles 3y, 4y, 5y and 120° meet at a point. Find y.

questions.q: Angles a, 47° and a lie on a straight line. Find a.
questions.model: 2a + 47 = 180 (angles on a straight line). 2a = 133, so a = 66.5°.

questions.q: Angles x, x + 40, 2x and 80° meet at a point. Find x.
A pupil writes 'x = 70° because it looks like it'. Why does this earn no marks?
questions.a: Diagrams are not drawn to scale; a reason must be an angle fact.

questions.q: (a) Angles (x + 15)°, 2x° and 75° lie on a straight line: find x. (b) Angles 5p°, 3p°, 90° and 110° meet at a point: find p. (c) Two lines cross; one angle is (3t - 10)° and the opposite angle is (t + 50)°: find t and all four angles.
questions.model: (a) x + 15 + 2x + 75 = 180 (angles on a straight line). 3x + 90 = 180, 3x = 90, x = 30.

questions.q: The angles at a point are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. The smallest lies on a straight line with angle y. Find y.
Write your own two-step angle problem with a full solution and reasons; swap with a partner to check.
questions.a: Own problem; the partner checks every reason.

Why must every step have a reason?
questions.a: Diagrams are not to scale; the reason shows the step is true.

questions.q: Big question: how do you choose which angle fact to use first?
questions.a: Look for an angle linked to one you know by a fact (line, point or opposite); find unlabelled angles on the way.
